items.title: 如何用 FFmpeg 把 MOV 转 MP4：编码一致时直接流复制
items.title_orig: How to Convert MOV to MP4 With FFmpeg: Stream-Copy When the Codec Already Matches, and Re-Encode Only When It Doesn't
items.summary: 若视频已是 H.264、音频为 AAC，用 -c copy 重封装即可；ProRes、DNxHR 等需重新编码。
items.summary_orig: Short answer: to turn a QuickTime .mov into an .mp4 , start with -c copy . If the file is already H.264 video plus AAC audio, stream copy remuxes the packets, the first-frame RGB24 md5 stays the same, and the duration does not change. If the video is ProRes, DNxHR, or another codec that MP4 players will not handle, you have to re-encode.

Their ancient relatives were very different animals.

items.summary_orig: Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic and the same fault can produce different execution traces on different runs. Unmesh Joshi describes how deterministic simulation testing addresses this by replacing real clocks, networks, and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop.

items.summary_orig: wf-verify: One Verify Gate for Every Ecosystem Agentic loops break down at the verify step. The agent writes code, then either skips verification or runs a command that only covers one ecosystem. A Go repo gets go test ; a Bun repo gets bun test ; a mixed repo gets nothing consistent. items.summary_orig: OpenCode Workflow Loop: spec → implement → verify → review → ship Vibe-coding gets you a demo. It rarely gets you a shippable repo. The gap is not the model; it is the missing structure around the model: a spec to aim at, a verify gate to catch regressions, a review pass to catch the things tests do not, and a ship step that does not skip the boring parts.

items.summary_orig: A classifier that says it is 90% sure should be right about 90% of the time. That sounds like a low bar, and yet most modern neural networks fail it badly.
